title: Prompt Evaluation Harness
summary: Build a deterministic eval harness that scores model outputs against a labeled test set using multiple criteria, and flags regressions between two prompt versions.
requirements: Accept a labeled test set (input + a per-case checkable criterion function).
Run each case against a model function, catching failures from both the model call AND the checker.
Compute an aggregate score and compare against an optional recorded baseline.
Flag a regression when the new score is below the baseline.
start: Start from Module 7's exercise function and wire it to a small real labeled test set for a task you care about (e.g. 5-10 hand-written prompt/expected-output pairs), instead of the synthetic mock functions used in the exercise.
acceptance: All test cases passing produces a score of 1.0 and no regression (with no baseline).
A mix of pass/fail cases produces the correct score and correctly identifies exactly which cases failed.
A model_fn that raises for one case is caught and counted as a failure without crashing the other cases.
A check() function that raises for one case is caught and counted as a failure without crashing the other cases.
A score below a provided baseline is correctly flagged as a regression; a score at or above baseline is not.
tests: 5/5 cases pass → score 1.0, regression false (no baseline).
2/4 cases pass → score 0.5, results list correctly flags which 2 failed.
model_fn raises for 1 of 3 cases → that case fails, the other 2 are evaluated normally.
check() raises for 1 of 2 cases → that case fails, the other case is evaluated normally.
Score 0.6 vs baseline 0.75 → regression true. Score 0.8 vs baseline 0.75 → regression false.
mistakes: Not wrapping the check() call in its own try/except, letting one bad checker crash the whole run.
Computing score as pass_count/total without guarding total=0 (division by zero).
Treating an unchanged score as a regression instead of using a strict less-than comparison.
solution: Loop over test cases: try the model_fn call in a try/except, mark failed if it raises.
Separately try the check() call in its own try/except, mark failed if it raises.
Compare against baseline (if provided) using strict less-than for the regression flag.
